pathway.title: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Corporate leverage is moderate on the issuer's own basis, but reported figures flatter it and the guidance cut pushes it higher. Corporate debt, net was 3.41x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, yet that EBITDA includes net construction recognitions of USD 218 million; measured on principal net of cash and without them, corporate leverage is 3.88x, and at the low end, midpoint and high end of the cut 2026 guidance it is 4.05x, 4.02x and 4.00x. A further USD 100 million shortfall against the midpoint would lift it to 4.40x. The company reports total net leverage of about 3.9x without printing its definition or any covenant level, so the cushion to a maintenance test cannot be measured. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10

Cash conversion is weak against the earnings reported and is being outrun by shareholder returns. Last-twelve-months free cash flow was 27.75% of adjusted EBITDA, nine-month adjusted free cash flow fell 39.77% to USD 206 million and covered only 50.24% of buybacks, and buybacks plus Elara exceeded free cash flow by USD 240 million. The gap was met with corporate borrowing: net corporate debt proceeds were USD 339 million, revolver drawings rose by USD 360 million, and cash plus remaining revolver capacity fell 34.73% to USD 684 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22, 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 18; calculation C14; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C24

Sales are the weak link, and selling costs are not flexing with them. Contract sales fell 11.03% in the third quarter on volume per guest down 12.46%, while net sales and marketing cost rose 6.86% in nine months and took 52.70% of each dollar of contract sales against 46.79% a year earlier, so operating leverage is working in reverse. The first half was down only 1.67%, so the deterioration is recent; management says its initiatives are ramping more slowly than planned, and the midpoint of 2026 EBITDA guidance was cut by 5.82%. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C27; calculation C26; calculation C25; calculation C29; calculation C33

Receivables funding supports the credit, but the collateral is weaker than its carrying value suggests and the allowance was lowered. Non-recourse debt equals 78.65% of timeshare financing receivables and is payable only from them, originated receivables carry a weighted 14.2% rate against a funding cost 9.15 percentage points lower, and gross originated receivables grew 12.63% in nine months. Against that, 12.04% of originated receivables had stopped accruing interest, up from 11.73%, 11.17% were 121 days or more past due, up from 10.86%, and the allowance fell to 28.42% of the gross balance from 29.41% after a method change that released USD 55 million, so reported earnings include some reserve release. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, 25; calculation C13; calculation C45; calculation C44; calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C36; calculation C37

A recurring earnings base and a long-dated franchise cushion the downside. Resort operations and club management earned segment adjusted EBITDA of USD 440 million, level with USD 441 million a year earlier and 31.01% of segment EBITDA, on cost-plus management fees that the company calls highly predictable, and the exclusive Hilton licence runs far beyond every debt maturity. The price is a licence fee that steps up on Bluegreen revenue from 2027, and capital spending is light at 6.68% of adjusted EBITDA, which leaves little extra to cut in a downturn. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C28; calculation C34

Refinancing capacity is adequate near term but depends on the receivables markets and on sales stabilising. Only 27.01% of corporate principal falls due by the end of 2029, the Term Loan B due 2028 was refinanced into 2033 at unchanged pricing, and receivables warehouses were renewed or opened in 2026. The senior notes due 2029 are 17.19% of corporate principal, the Term Loan A falls due in 2028 and the revolver in 2030, so the first test is whether they can be refinanced on similar terms if leverage is above 4.00x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 23, 25, 26; calculation C46; calculation C47; calculation C48

Financial policy is the weakest dimension, and governance can be judged only in part. The company bought back stock from the underwriters in both Apollo offerings, approved a second repurchase plan in August 2026 and states no plan to pay dividends, so cash returns to shareholders rank ahead of debt reduction; the sponsor's holding after its June 2026 sale and the board and pay arrangements are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 165

runs.text: The strongest support is receivables funding that does not claim on corporate cash flow. Non-recourse debt is payable only from pledged receivables, the receivables yield a weighted 14.2% against a lower funding cost, and the warehouses were renewed or opened in 2026, so growth in receivables does not add corporate debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 20, 24, 25; calculation C13; calculation C45

The second support is a recurring earnings stream. Resort operations and club management earn cost-plus fees on resort operating costs and held segment adjusted EBITDA at USD 440 million, so a part of EBITDA does not depend on selling new intervals. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 14; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C28

The third support is a long-dated exclusive franchise and a loyal buyer base. The Hilton licence runs far beyond every debt maturity with a non-compete, and existing owners made most contract sales, which lowers the cost of winning each sale. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 21, 22

The fourth support is a back-ended corporate maturity profile and light capital spending. Only 27.01% of corporate principal falls due by 2029 and capital spending is 6.68% of adjusted EBITDA, so there is no large investment programme competing for cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C47; calculation C34

The main weakness is sales conversion with sticky selling costs. Volume per guest fell 12.46% in the third quarter while net sales and marketing cost rose, so each dollar of contract sales now carries more cost, which cuts EBITDA and the cash available for debt service. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C31; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

The second weakness is shareholder returns funded with corporate debt. Buybacks and Elara exceeded free cash flow, corporate borrowing and revolver drawings rose, and liquidity fell, which leaves less room to absorb a further fall in sales. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22, 23; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C24

The third weakness is earnings quality. Net construction recognitions and a lower allowance lifted third-quarter earnings, so reported leverage understates the stress; on a clean basis corporate leverage is 3.88x and about 4.02x at the guidance midpoint. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C4; calculation C6

The fourth weakness is the quality of the receivables behind the funding. Non-accrual and long-dated delinquency rose and the allowance ratio fell, so the collateral may produce less cash than the carrying value implies if the economy weakens. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18; calculation C38; calculation C40; calculation C36

The fifth weakness is dependence on one licensor and a sponsor that is selling down. Hilton sets the brand, fee and product rights, the fee step-up on Bluegreen revenue begins in 2027, and governance alignment cannot be tested without the proxy statement. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 23, 165

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The acquisitions that shape the balance sheet are Diamond Resorts in August 2021, Bluegreen Vacations in January 2024 and the remaining 75% of Elara in April 2026. Diamond was paid for in HGV shares, which left funds controlled by Apollo and other former owners with 28% of the company at completion. Bluegreen was an all-cash transaction worth USD 1.6 billion including net debt, and it brought the Big Cedar joint venture, a ten-year exclusive Bass Pro marketing agreement that took effect on the same date, and the reduced Hilton fee on Bluegreen revenue. Elara, a joint venture in which the company held 25%, was bought on April 29, 2026 for USD 131 million of cash after an announced price of USD 129 million, and it added USD 411 million of timeshare receivables and USD 310 million of non-recourse debt, with goodwill of USD 2 million on preliminary accounting. In the second quarter the company also sold its interests in certain resort properties under an agreement dated April 24, 2026, booking a loss of USD 48 million and keeping a right to share in future sale proceeds. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 38, 132; EX-99.1_2026-04-30_hgvq12026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-03-31_hgv-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 35, 36

Debt issued or reset in 2026 is mostly non-recourse receivables funding. A securitization of USD 500 million of timeshare loans closed on April 16, 2026 at an overall weighted average rate of 5.13%, and a second of about USD 300 million followed in June. The Timeshare Facility was renewed in May at USD 1.0 billion with a commitment period to May 2028 and maturity to May 2029, and a USD 200 million warehouse facility for the Big Cedar receivables was entered into on September 14. The only corporate change was on July 17, when the Term Loan B due 2028 was refinanced into an amended USD 850 million Term Loan B due 2033 at an unchanged margin of SOFR plus 2.00%, and the documents read show no new corporate notes in 2026. Funding access for receivables is therefore the dependency creditors should watch, because it carries the growth that corporate debt does not. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_hgv-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (issuer id hgv), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the seven supplied filings and earnings releases can support the Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit modules, and what they cannot support. No evidence outside the seven sources was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied handoffs: none; Source readiness is the first module of this run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The seven supplied documents support a source-based credit snapshot of Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. to its September 30, 2026 balance sheet, but covenant headroom and the guarantor perimeter cannot be established without executed debt documents, and governance is only partly covered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Income statements, and through the releases cash flow statements, cover every quarter from the first quarter of 2025 to the third quarter of 2026, with the fourth quarter of 2025 by subtraction. Third-quarter 2026 earnings include a $296 million net construction recognition and a $55 million allowance reduction booked as a change in estimate, so quarters are not comparable without the company's reconciling table. The 3.9x total net leverage the company reports is not defined or reconciled in any supplied document.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16, 23–24; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 165–166; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These checks tie the supplied statements to each other; they are consistency checks on the sources, not credit analysis. Amounts are USD millions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed credit agreement, its 2026-07-17 amendment and the note indentures were not supplied, and no supplied document prints a covenant level. The annual and quarterly reports state only that the issuer complied with all applicable maintenance and financial covenants, so covenant definitions, headroom, baskets and the guarantor perimeter cannot be established, and Fundamental credit is limited to company-stated compliance. The gap is material. Adding the credit agreement with Amendment No. 10 and the indentures would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, and Part III of the annual report is incorporated from it. Board independence, executive pay, the full beneficial ownership table and related-party terms beyond the financial statement notes are therefore not established. The annual report and the later quarterly reports do state the main sponsor facts: funds affiliated with Apollo held 18,245,825 shares at 2026-02-19 with board designation rights that step down as the holding falls, and Apollo-managed entities sold 5,000,000 shares in June 2026 with a 750,000-share option exercised on 2026-06-22, but the sponsor's holding after that sale is not stated. Business & governance is therefore limited on governance and current ownership. The gap is material. Adding the proxy statement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No credit rating, rating agency document, market quote, peer financial data, fund limit or earlier run was supplied. The requested modules can run without them, but rating and market context, relative value and portfolio fit cannot be assessed from this set. The gap is minor for this pathway.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company reports total net leverage of about 3.9x at 2026-09-30, 3.8x at 2026-06-30 and 3.9x at 2026-03-31, but no supplied document defines the ratio or reconciles its debt and EBITDA inputs, and no year-end 2025 figure is printed. Financial foundation has to calculate leverage on stated bases and treat the reported ratio as a company comparator only. The gap is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third-quarter 2026 results include a net construction recognition of USD 296 million on a Hawaii project and a USD 55 million reduction in the allowance for originated receivables booked as a prospective change in estimate, while every quarter of 2025 and the first two quarters of 2026 carry net deferrals. The consolidated statements also include securitisation vehicles carrying non-recourse debt, and Elara has been consolidated since 2026-04-29 with preliminary purchase accounting. Reported quarterly earnings and leverage are therefore not like-for-like across periods or perimeters unless the release's deferral table and the corporate versus non-recourse split are used. The sources carry those tables, so this is a comparability limit rather than a missing source, and it is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's other adjustment items are shown as one line in each reconciliation, described only as restructuring, one-time charges, other non-cash items and purchase accounting amortisation. Their components and whether they have been realised are not itemised in any supplied document, which limits the add-back bridge in Financial foundation. The gap is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release and no 2025 interim balance sheets were supplied. Apart from the adjusted EBITDA table, which prints fourth-quarter 2025 net income, interest, tax, depreciation and adjusted EBITDA, fourth-quarter 2025 income and cash flow items can be obtained only by subtracting nine months from the year, a method that agrees with the printed adjusted EBITDA for that quarter, and the balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not available (only equity, allowance and cash balances at those dates appear in comparatives), so a leverage trend through 2025 cannot be built from period-end debt. The gap is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third-quarter report has no subsequent events note, and the set ends at 2026-10-29, so events from 2026-10-30 to the 2026-11-05 cutoff are not covered. The credit agreement amendment of 2026-07-17 and the receivables loan amendment of 2026-05-20 are cited as current reports that were not supplied. The gap is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Presentation differs between filings. The balance of USD 851 million at 2025-12-31 is labelled Term Loan B due 2028 in the annual report and Term Loan B due 2033 in the third-quarter comparative, and the second-quarter report explains that the Term Loan B due 2028 was refinanced into an amended USD 850 million Term Loan B due 2033 on 2026-07-17. The amount is the same, so this is a relabelling after the refinancing and not a conflict in value. It is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (issuer id hgv), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: Financial foundation, meaning normalised statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage on the supplied sources. No evidence outside the seven sources and the Source readiness result was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate creditors face leverage of 3.41x adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, but most of this year's fall in reported leverage comes from construction accounting timing, so credit quality has not improved as much as the headline suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Consolidated debt including non-recourse securitisation funding was USD 7,776 million, or 6.52x reported EBITDA against 9.55x at the end of 2025, and USD 2,891 million of it is payable from pledged receivables rather than from corporate cash flow. Last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA includes a net construction recognition of USD 218 million, against net deferrals of USD 202 million in 2025. Excluding that timing, corporate leverage is 3.88x, close to the 3.9x the company reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 22, 24; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C28; calculation C45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two different claims sit in the consolidated balance sheet. Corporate debt, net was USD 4,885 million at September 30, 2026, which is 3.41x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA and 3.25x after unrestricted cash, and it is the revolver, term loans and senior notes that rank against the issuer. Non-recourse debt, net was a further USD 2,891 million, equal to 78.65% of the USD 3,676 million of timeshare financing receivables and payable only from the receivables pledged to it, so the consolidated 6.52x and 6.33x net describe a mixed pool. A corporate creditor should therefore read the corporate ratios and treat the non-recourse pool as a funding line whose commitment periods end in 2028 and must be renewed or replaced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings recovery in reported figures is mostly timing. Deferred revenue, which holds customer sales on projects still under construction, fell from USD 637 million at the end of 2025 to USD 263 million at September 30, 2026 as a Hawaii project was completed, and the third quarter recognised a net construction benefit of USD 296 million, lifting adjusted EBITDA for the quarter to USD 617 million. Operating cash flow in the same quarter was USD 87 million, so the earnings came from sales booked in earlier periods rather than from cash earned in the quarter. The float had grown from USD 252 million at the end of 2024, and last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,434 million carries USD 218 million of net recognition that is not a quarterly run rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 7; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover on reported EBITDA improved to 4.22x from 2.56x at the end of 2025, and on adjusted EBITDA to 5.07x from 3.26x, while cash interest on corporate debt fell to USD 283 million over the last twelve months from USD 297 million in 2025. Lower interest helped, but the numerator moved far more than the denominator, and free cash flow of USD 398 million over the last twelve months against adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,434 million shows that cash conversion is well below the earnings figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C21; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity has been used while earnings looked stronger. Revolver borrowings rose from USD 130 million at the end of 2025 to USD 490 million at September 30, 2026 in the nine months in which the issuer repurchased USD 410 million of shares and paid USD 103 million for Elara, and remaining revolver capacity fell from USD 809 million to USD 457 million. Cash plus remaining revolver capacity was USD 684 million, against USD 1,048 million at year-end, and the USD 450 million and USD 175 million of warehouse capacity is non-recourse receivables funding rather than corporate liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22, 23, 25; calculation C37; calculation C36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The corporate maturity wall is back-ended but concentrated in 2029. Corporate principal due is USD 6 million in the last three months of 2026 and USD 22 million in 2027, then USD 430 million in 2028 and USD 878 million in 2029, when the senior notes due 2029 fall due, followed by USD 515 million in 2030 and USD 3,095 million after that. Refinancing therefore depends on earnings holding up, which is why the construction-timing distortion matters to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own figure: total net leverage of 3.9x, 3.8x and 3.9x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, and a deferral-excluded calculation that gives 3.73x at the end of 2025 and 3.88x now, so corporate leverage on its own basis is broadly flat, neither improving nor worsening. Resort and club management earned USD 440 million of segment adjusted EBITDA in nine months, level with the prior year, which supports the recurring base. The view would change if covenant levels in the credit agreement show thin headroom on the issuer's definition, if contract sales keep falling (USD 807 million in the quarter against USD 907 million), or if the net leverage definition proves to exclude items counted here.

Severity: Low. The 2025 quarterly reports and the fourth-quarter release would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carrying values by instrument, the revolver commitment and margin, interest floors, scheduled amortisation, the months in which the term loan B tranches and the notes mature, and security packages beyond the labels in the debt tables are not printed. The debt instruments register states each as not supplied. Severity: Medium. It limits maturity-month analysis and any claim on amortisation. The credit agreement and indentures would close it.

fields.name: Quote

Severity: Medium. It limits any statement of structural priority. The credit agreement and indentures would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No covenant level, definition or headroom is printed in any supplied source; the reports state compliance with all applicable maintenance and financial covenants and ratios only. Covenant capacity is not calculable and none is inferred. Severity: High. The credit agreement and its amendments would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer reports total net leverage of about 3.9x at 2026-03-31, 3.8x at 2026-06-30 and 3.9x at 2026-09-30, but no source defines the ratio or reconciles its debt and EBITDA, and no year-end 2025 figure is printed. The proxy calculation of 3.88x is labelled Analyst Judgement and is not the issuer's figure. Severity: Medium. It limits the comparison with the issuer's own leverage. A definition from the issuer or the credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third-quarter 2026 earnings include a net construction recognition of USD 296 million and a USD 55 million reduction in the allowance for originated receivables booked as a change in estimate, and Elara has been consolidated since 2026-04-29 with preliminary purchase accounting. Last-twelve-months ratios therefore mix periods and perimeters and are not like-for-like with 2025. Severity: Medium. The issuer's deferral table and the corporate and non-recourse split are used beside every consolidated ratio, and the final Elara accounting would close the perimeter point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opening cash for the first quarter of 2025 is 765 in the first-quarter 2026 report and 766 in the annual report and the second-quarter release, a difference of USD 1 million that is not reconciled. Severity: Low. Each column keeps its own filing's figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow as the issuer defines it is printed for quarters and nine months but not for fiscal years, and year-end member counts are printed only as more than 720,000, so those cells are not supplied. Severity: Low. The annual figure is calculated in the financial metrics table and labelled.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt: operating lease liabilities of USD 106 million sit on their own balance sheet line and are not in total debt, inventory purchase commitments are USD 304 million, surety bond commitments are USD 346 million, and legal accruals are USD 19 million; no pension or retiree medical obligation is printed. Severity: Low. None is added to debt or net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The non-debt funding float in deferred revenue and advanced deposits is flagged: deferred revenue was USD 263 million and advanced deposits USD 225 million at 2026-09-30, against USD 637 million and USD 228 million at 2025-12-31, and its fall reflects recognition on project completion rather than cash repayment. Severity: Medium. The float should be watched as new projects defer sales again.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (issuer id hgv), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is Business & governance: the business model, ownership and control, sponsor and governance facts, and the transactions and new debt of 2024 to 2026, read from the seven supplied sources and the Source readiness result only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations has a durable licensed franchise, but sales are falling, receivables funding must keep rolling and the sponsor is selling down while the company buys back stock, so creditors carry execution risk more than franchise risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: About 73% of contract sales come from existing owners, resort management earns cost-plus fees, and the initial term of the Hilton licence has about 90 years to run. Against that, contract sales fell to USD 807 million in the third quarter from USD 907 million, guidance was cut by 5.82% at the midpoint, the discounted Hilton fee on Bluegreen revenue steps up to 5% in the fourth year after the 2024 closing, and a second USD 600 million repurchase plan was approved in August 2026. Governance is only partly assessable because the proxy statement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 21, 22, 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19; calculation C18; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise is long-dated and exclusive, but it rests on one licensor and the fee is a growing claim on revenue. Hilton kept no ownership after the 2017 spin-off, the initial licence term has about 90 years to run with exclusivity in vacation ownership for about 25 years, and the fee is 5% of gross revenues, with license fee expense equal to 4.24% of total revenues in 2025. Reduced fees of 2% to 4% on acquired Diamond and Bluegreen revenue climb to 5%, and if annual rebranding milestones are missed the company owes an escalated fee of up to an additional 1%, while missed cumulative targets would let Hilton bar sales of its HGV Max product. The Bluegreen discount is the nearer risk because the fourth year after the January 2024 closing begins in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6, 21, 22, 23, 113; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customers are loyal but are buying less per tour, and management has acknowledged it. Existing owners made 74% of contract sales in 2025 and 73% in the nine months to September 30, 2026, and tour flow rose 1.7% in the third quarter, but volume per guest fell 12.5%, so contract sales were USD 2,336 million for nine months against USD 2,462 million and USD 807 million in the quarter against USD 907 million. The chief executive said the sales initiatives are taking longer to ramp than expected, guidance for 2026 adjusted EBITDA excluding deferrals and recognitions was cut by 5.82% at the midpoint, and a promotion to chief sales and marketing officer was announced on the same day. The member base is also slightly smaller, down 0.78% from a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 19, 20; calculation C18; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor is exiting in steps, and its board and consent rights narrow as its stake falls. Apollo-managed holders sold shares in the fourth quarter of 2024, the third quarter of 2025 and June 2026, held 22.41% of the shares in February 2026, and in the two underwritten offerings the company bought back shares from the underwriters for USD 40 million and USD 38 million. The stockholders agreement gives Apollo two board seats, falling to one and then none as its holding drops through two thresholds, and a consent right over some charter changes and board size while it holds at least the lower threshold. In February 2026 the holding exceeded the higher threshold by only a small margin, so if all shares sold in June had counted towards it one seat would have lapsed while the consent right would remain, but the filings do not state the holding after that sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 28, 69, 157; 10-Q_2026-06-30_hgv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation favours shareholders over debt reduction. The company repurchased USD 600 million of stock in 2025 and USD 410 million in the nine months to September 30, 2026, against USD 450 million in the same months of 2025, and a second USD 600 million plan approved on August 12, 2026 starts once the USD 17 million left under the current plan is used. The filings state no plan to pay cash dividends, so buybacks, including those that absorb sponsor sales, are the shareholder-return channel and compete with creditors for the same cash. The share count fell 6.88% between February and October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisitions explain the debt and the perimeter, and the latest one brought its own non-recourse funding. Bluegreen cost USD 1.6 billion including net debt in January 2024, was paid in cash and brought the Big Cedar joint venture, in which the company holds 51%, although the documents read do not detail its acquired balance sheet. Elara, bought on April 29, 2026 for USD 131 million of cash, added USD 411 million of timeshare receivables and USD 310 million of non-recourse debt, so most of its funding does not rank against corporate creditors, although the purchase accounting is still preliminary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New borrowing in 2026 is mostly receivables funding, and the one corporate change extended maturities at unchanged pricing. The company closed securitizations of about USD 500 million and USD 300 million of receivables in April and June, renewed its warehouse facility to USD 1.0 billion, opened a USD 200 million facility for the Big Cedar receivables in September, and on July 17 refinanced the Term Loan B due 2028 into a USD 850 million Term Loan B due 2033 at the same margin of SOFR plus 2.00%. Access to the receivables markets therefore carries the growth that corporate debt does not, which is the dependency creditors should watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is the earnings base that does not depend on sales: resort operations and club management earned USD 440 million of segment adjusted EBITDA in the nine months, level with USD 441 million a year earlier, on cost-plus fees that the company describes as highly predictable. The licence is long and exclusive, existing owners are most of the buyers, and the chief executive reports initial signs of progress as the third quarter ended. The view would weaken if contract sales fall again in the fourth quarter, if the Bluegreen fee step-up arrives before sales recover, or if the proxy statement shows board or pay arrangements that favour shareholders over creditors. It would strengthen if volume per guest recovers, repurchases slow while corporate debt is paid down, and the sponsor's remaining holding and board rights are shown to be settled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that creditors face execution rather than governance risk rests on the annual report's account of the stockholders agreement and the signature page, and board independence, pay arrangements and director shareholdings could change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sponsor's holding after the June 2026 offering is not stated, so the conclusion that its board rights are narrowing cannot show whether a seat has already lapsed or whether the consent right is still in force.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Hilton licence text is not supplied, so the timing and size of the Bluegreen fee step-up are derived from the annual report summary and the closing date, and the conclusion on fee pressure could change if minimum fees or escalation apply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Elara purchase accounting is preliminary and may change for up to a year after closing, which would alter the conclusion that the acquisition added mostly non-recourse debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisitions that shape the balance sheet are Diamond Resorts in August 2021, Bluegreen Vacations in January 2024 and the remaining 75% of Elara in April 2026. Diamond was paid for in HGV shares, which left funds controlled by Apollo and other former owners with 28% of the company at completion. Bluegreen was an all-cash transaction worth USD 1.6 billion including net debt, and it brought the Big Cedar joint venture, a ten-year exclusive Bass Pro marketing agreement that took effect on the same date, and the reduced Hilton fee on Bluegreen revenue. Elara, a joint venture in which the company held 25%, was bought on April 29, 2026 for USD 131 million of cash after an announced price of USD 129 million, and it added USD 411 million of timeshare receivables and USD 310 million of non-recourse debt, with goodwill of USD 2 million on preliminary accounting. In the second quarter the company also sold its interests in certain resort properties under an agreement dated April 24, 2026, booking a loss of USD 48 million and keeping a right to share in future sale proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt issued or reset in 2026 is mostly non-recourse receivables funding. A securitization of USD 500 million of timeshare loans closed on April 16, 2026 at an overall weighted average rate of 5.13%, and a second of about USD 300 million followed in June. The Timeshare Facility was renewed in May at USD 1.0 billion with a commitment period to May 2028 and maturity to May 2029, and a USD 200 million warehouse facility for the Big Cedar receivables was entered into on September 14. The only corporate change was on July 17, when the Term Loan B due 2028 was refinanced into an amended USD 850 million Term Loan B due 2033 at an unchanged margin of SOFR plus 2.00%, and the documents read show no new corporate notes in 2026. Funding access for receivables is therefore the dependency creditors should watch, because it carries the growth that corporate debt does not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (issuer id hgv), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is Fundamental credit: a synthesis of business quality, cash conversion, liquidity, refinancing capacity, receivables funding and financial policy, read from the seven supplied sources and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied handoffs: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 c75b075a7f15378fcffc89e81e7281263bbd9e6694fe95c7eaf13641419dd828; Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 4489e7ddf5c2e19b51316652beb28024b0b820ce7e449e642b91fc658aa419fe; Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 287b729b1b68aa6cdf6bfa6923a983dbee8d71c49e509038f4f3fee6c9a05963.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations has an adequate but weakening corporate credit profile: leverage is supportable on recurring fees and non-recourse receivables funding, but falling sales and debt-funded buybacks are eroding the cushion creditors rely on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate net debt was 3.88x EBITDA excluding construction timing at September 30, 2026 and would be 4.02x at the midpoint of the cut 2026 guidance. In nine months the company raised a net USD 339 million of corporate debt while spending USD 410 million on buybacks and USD 103 million on Elara, and cash plus revolver capacity fell to USD 684 million from USD 1,048 million. The USD 2,891 million of non-recourse debt is payable only from pledged receivables and is not a claim on corporate cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C17; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate leverage is moderate on the issuer's own basis, but reported figures flatter it and the guidance cut pushes it higher. Corporate debt, net was 3.41x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, yet that EBITDA includes net construction recognitions of USD 218 million; measured on principal net of cash and without them, corporate leverage is 3.88x, and at the low end, midpoint and high end of the cut 2026 guidance it is 4.05x, 4.02x and 4.00x. A further USD 100 million shortfall against the midpoint would lift it to 4.40x. The company reports total net leverage of about 3.9x without printing its definition or any covenant level, so the cushion to a maintenance test cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is weak against the earnings reported and is being outrun by shareholder returns. Last-twelve-months free cash flow was 27.75% of adjusted EBITDA, nine-month adjusted free cash flow fell 39.77% to USD 206 million and covered only 50.24% of buybacks, and buybacks plus Elara exceeded free cash flow by USD 240 million. The gap was met with corporate borrowing: net corporate debt proceeds were USD 339 million, revolver drawings rose by USD 360 million, and cash plus remaining revolver capacity fell 34.73% to USD 684 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22, 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 18; calculation C14; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sales are the weak link, and selling costs are not flexing with them. Contract sales fell 11.03% in the third quarter on volume per guest down 12.46%, while net sales and marketing cost rose 6.86% in nine months and took 52.70% of each dollar of contract sales against 46.79% a year earlier, so operating leverage is working in reverse. The first half was down only 1.67%, so the deterioration is recent; management says its initiatives are ramping more slowly than planned, and the midpoint of 2026 EBITDA guidance was cut by 5.82%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C27; calculation C26; calculation C25; calculation C29; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Receivables funding supports the credit, but the collateral is weaker than its carrying value suggests and the allowance was lowered. Non-recourse debt equals 78.65% of timeshare financing receivables and is payable only from them, originated receivables carry a weighted 14.2% rate against a funding cost 9.15 percentage points lower, and gross originated receivables grew 12.63% in nine months. Against that, 12.04% of originated receivables had stopped accruing interest, up from 11.73%, 11.17% were 121 days or more past due, up from 10.86%, and the allowance fell to 28.42% of the gross balance from 29.41% after a method change that released USD 55 million, so reported earnings include some reserve release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, 25; calculation C13; calculation C45; calculation C44; calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C36; calculation C37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A recurring earnings base and a long-dated franchise cushion the downside. Resort operations and club management earned segment adjusted EBITDA of USD 440 million, level with USD 441 million a year earlier and 31.01% of segment EBITDA, on cost-plus management fees that the company calls highly predictable, and the exclusive Hilton licence runs far beyond every debt maturity. The price is a licence fee that steps up on Bluegreen revenue from 2027, and capital spending is light at 6.68% of adjusted EBITDA, which leaves little extra to cut in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hgv-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C28; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity is adequate near term but depends on the receivables markets and on sales stabilising. Only 27.01% of corporate principal falls due by the end of 2029, the Term Loan B due 2028 was refinanced into 2033 at unchanged pricing, and receivables warehouses were renewed or opened in 2026. The senior notes due 2029 are 17.19% of corporate principal, the Term Loan A falls due in 2028 and the revolver in 2030, so the first test is whether they can be refinanced on similar terms if leverage is above 4.00x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 23, 25, 26; calculation C46; calculation C47; calculation C48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension, and governance can be judged only in part. The company bought back stock from the underwriters in both Apollo offerings, approved a second repurchase plan in August 2026 and states no plan to pay dividends, so cash returns to shareholders rank ahead of debt reduction; the sponsor's holding after its June 2026 sale and the board and pay arrangements are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that debt service is comfortable and the pressure is largely discretionary: interest cover is 5.07x on adjusted EBITDA and 4.30x without construction recognitions, corporate maturities through 2027 are small, nine-month free cash flow of USD 273 million is far above the USD 29 million of a year earlier, buybacks can be stopped at the board's choice, and the chief executive reports initial signs of progress as the third quarter ended. The view would improve if contract sales stabilise, repurchases pause while the revolver is repaid and non-accrual receivables stop rising. It would weaken if fourth-quarter contract sales fall further, guidance is cut again, revolver drawings rise to fund buybacks, or receivable delinquency keeps climbing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 17, 18; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No covenant level, definition or headroom is printed in any supplied document, so the conclusion that leverage near 4.02x is supportable cannot be tested against a maintenance test and the cushion could be thinner than it looks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 4.02x reading at the guidance midpoint divides September 30 debt by full-year 2026 EBITDA excluding deferrals, which mixes dates and definitions, so the conclusion that guidance pushes corporate leverage above 4.00x is indicative rather than exact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer, rating or market pricing evidence is supplied, so the judgements on scale, competitive position and refinancing access compare the issuer only with its own history and could move against peers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Securitization trigger levels, pool-level excess spread and vintage performance are not supplied, so the conclusion that receivables funding is a support rests on balance sheet delinquency data and could weaken if triggers are close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is receivables funding that does not claim on corporate cash flow. Non-recourse debt is payable only from pledged receivables, the receivables yield a weighted 14.2% against a lower funding cost, and the warehouses were renewed or opened in 2026, so growth in receivables does not add corporate debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 20, 24, 25; calculation C13; calculation C45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second support is a recurring earnings stream. Resort operations and club management earn cost-plus fees on resort operating costs and held segment adjusted EBITDA at USD 440 million, so a part of EBITDA does not depend on selling new intervals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third support is a long-dated exclusive franchise and a loyal buyer base. The Hilton licence runs far beyond every debt maturity with a non-compete, and existing owners made most contract sales, which lowers the cost of winning each sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth support is a back-ended corporate maturity profile and light capital spending. Only 27.01% of corporate principal falls due by 2029 and capital spending is 6.68% of adjusted EBITDA, so there is no large investment programme competing for cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C47; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is sales conversion with sticky selling costs. Volume per guest fell 12.46% in the third quarter while net sales and marketing cost rose, so each dollar of contract sales now carries more cost, which cuts EBITDA and the cash available for debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C31; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is shareholder returns funded with corporate debt. Buybacks and Elara exceeded free cash flow, corporate borrowing and revolver drawings rose, and liquidity fell, which leaves less room to absorb a further fall in sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22, 23; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is earnings quality. Net construction recognitions and a lower allowance lifted third-quarter earnings, so reported leverage understates the stress; on a clean basis corporate leverage is 3.88x and about 4.02x at the guidance midpoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C4; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is the quality of the receivables behind the funding. Non-accrual and long-dated delinquency rose and the allowance ratio fell, so the collateral may produce less cash than the carrying value implies if the economy weakens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18; calculation C38; calculation C40; calculation C36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is dependence on one licensor and a sponsor that is selling down. Hilton sets the brand, fee and product rights, the fee step-up on Bluegreen revenue begins in 2027, and governance alignment cannot be tested without the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hilton Grand Vacations sells and finances timeshare vacation ownership intervals under a Hilton licence and earns fees from managing resorts and clubs. Sales of intervals are the largest revenue line and the most cyclical, financing and management fees are recurring, and rental of unsold inventory runs below its direct cost, so the business is moderately cyclical and the recurring lines carry the debt service in a weak sales year. Properties are concentrated in Florida, Europe, Hawaii and a few other states, which ties cash flow to leisure travel demand in those destinations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly listed, and the annual report describes Apollo as a significant stockholder rather than a controlling owner. Funds affiliated with Apollo hold designation and consent rights that narrow as the holding falls, Hilton owns no shares, and non-recourse securitization vehicles are consolidated but their debt is not a legal liability of the issuer. The credit consequence is that sponsor control risk is receding while the company's own buybacks and the sponsor's share sales interact, and the proxy statement is needed to test board alignment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue rests on repeat owners and on financing: existing owners made most contract sales, and financing propensity rose to 70% from 66%, so each sale adds a receivable that earns interest and must be funded. The risk is that sales fell in the third quarter while more were financed, which grows the receivables to fund when volume is weakest; the implication is that funding market access matters more than usual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are largely fixed in the short run: 99 sales distribution centers, 146 Bass Pro locations with minimum annual payments and commitments to buy inventory over 12 years give little room to cut quickly, and net sales and marketing cost rose while sales fell. Operating leverage therefore works against margins in a downturn, which is the main reason EBITDA is more volatile than revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C25; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is unstable because deferred revenue and net construction recognitions move earnings away from cash. Third-quarter operating cash flow was far below the earnings recognised, and last-twelve-months free cash flow is 27.75% of adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA overstates the cash available for debt service in this period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high: the industry is fragmented, competitors include other branded timeshare operators and hotel, cruise and home-sharing alternatives, and consolidation may create rivals with cheaper capital. The mechanism is pressure on tour efficiency and marketing cost, which shows in falling volume per guest, and the implication is that margins have limited protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New entrants face the barrier of brand, financing and sales distribution, and the Hilton non-compete keeps the licensor out of timeshare, which protects the franchise; substitutes are resorts, rentals and secondary-market resales, which cap pricing power and are a risk when consumers trade down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyers are consumers financed at a weighted 14.2% on originated loans, and most sales go to existing owners, which supports repeat sales but exposes the issuer to credit losses; suppliers include the licensor, developers who sell inventory and the asset-backed investors who fund receivables, and the licensor and investors have the most power over fees and funding cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and economic conditions are the credit-relevant PEST categories: marketing and sales are highly regulated with purchaser cancellation rights, and demand follows consumer confidence and the cost of financing. Political and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are receivables funding outside corporate debt, recurring management fees, an exclusive long licence and repeat owners; the weaknesses are sales conversion, selling cost rigidity, debt-funded buybacks and receivable quality; the opportunities that could improve credit are stabilising volume per guest and the integration of acquired properties into the Hilton brands; the threats are a weaker consumer, tighter securitization markets and the fee step-up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine dimensions are assessed as follows, using the strongest supported evidence for each.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and market position is Average: revenue of USD 5,937 million over the last twelve months and a large owner base give scale, but market share and peer comparison are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Competitive advantage is Average: the exclusive licence and repeat owners help, but volume per guest fell and the brand belongs to a third party.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business diversification is Weak: one licensed brand, one product family funded by the same buyers, and destinations concentrated in a few markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility is Average: capital spending is light but selling costs, minimum payments and inventory commitments are sticky.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin stability is Weak: net construction timing, a reserve release and falling conversion make margins volatile.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow stability is Weak: free cash flow swings with deferred revenue and covers only part of shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average: facilities were renewed and the Term Loan B extended, but 2029 concentration and reliance on securitization are risks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity position is Average: cash plus revolver capacity of USD 684 million is adequate against small near-term maturities but fell sharply in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance is Weak: buybacks funded with corporate debt, a sponsor sell-down and no proxy statement to test alignment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are non-recourse receivables funding and recurring fees, the constraints are cash conversion and policy, the trend is negative since the third quarter of 2026, and the missing datapoints are covenant terms, securitization triggers and peer data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the headwinds are weak sales conversion, the guidance cut, a fee step-up on Bluegreen revenue from 2027 and leverage near or above 4.00x; the tailwinds are the company's reported early progress, the option to stop buybacks and a sound maturity profile. The implication is that leverage depends on management's choice of capital allocation more than on near-term refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the refinancing of the 2028 Term Loan A, the 2029 senior notes and the revolver due 2030, the end of the licence-fee discount and the continued reliance on receivables markets decide credit quality, while rebranding of acquired properties and growth in recurring fees could lift stability. Sector tailwinds or headwinds beyond the issuer's own results are not supplied and are not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside starts with sales conversion staying at the third-quarter level, with volume per guest down and contract sales falling by about a tenth. Selling costs are largely fixed, so EBITDA excluding deferrals falls below the guided range; a further USD 100 million shortfall against the midpoint would lift corporate leverage to 4.40x. Free cash flow then falls short of buybacks again, the revolver absorbs the gap, and the liquidity of USD 684 million shrinks while the 2028 Term Loan A and 2029 notes approach. Management can stop buybacks, which carry USD 617 million of authorisation, cut inventory purchases where commitments allow cancellation, and slow receivable origination, and with corporate maturities of only USD 28 million through 2027 resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity event, but not to keep leverage near 3.9x without a change in capital allocation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hgv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 59; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_hgvq32026earningsreleaseex.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C10; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Hilton Grand Vacations presents an adequate business profile supported by non-recourse receivables funding, recurring management fees and an exclusive long licence, but credit quality is constrained by falling sales conversion, sticky selling costs and debt-funded buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because free cash flow swings with construction timing and covered only part of shareholder returns. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilising contract sales, the securitization markets and a pause in buybacks before the 2028 and 2029 maturities. The primary downside path is a further fall in sales conversion that lifts corporate leverage above 4.00x while the revolver funds buybacks. Further analysis would require covenant terms, securitization trigger levels, peer evidence and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: falling sales conversion with debt-funded buybacks.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6

Severity: Material. The securitization documents and trustee reports would close it.

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
